faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions about session tracking with OpenPanel.

items.question: Does OpenPanel have session replay?
items.answer: Yes, as an option in the web SDK. Turn on sessionReplay in the config and sessions get a recording next to their events, masked by default and kept 30 days. See the session replay page for the details.

items.question: Do I need to set up session tracking separately?
items.answer: No. Sessions are created automatically from the events and page views you already send. There's no separate session SDK or configuration step.

items.question: How does OpenPanel define a session?
items.answer: Events from the same device within 30 minutes of each other belong to one session. After 30 minutes without an event the session ends, and the server writes session_start and session_end itself. The device id is a hash of user agent, IP and site with a salt that rotates every day, so an anonymous visitor is a new device the next day; sessions are not stitched across days or devices unless the user is identified.

items.question: Can I see individual user sessions?
items.answer: Yes. The Sessions page lists every session with entry and exit page, duration, bounce, referrer, location, events and revenue. Open one to see the events in order, the visited pages, the profile when there is one, and the replay when it was recorded.

items.question: Does session tracking require cookies?
items.answer: No. Nothing is stored in a cookie or in localStorage. The device id is computed on the server from the request, with a salt that changes daily, which is why there is no consent banner to show.
